section_header: BODY ELECTRICAL SYSTEM — Instruments and Sender Gauges
title: Instruments and Sender Gauges Troubleshooting

content.description: Troubleshooting flowchart for speedometer with no display. Starts with checking if only speedometer is affected, then branches through multiple diagnostic steps including checking fuse GAUGE (7.5A) OK?, fuse blow conditions, vehicle side checks, fuel sender gauge terminal voltage check, tachometer connector voltage check, and shorts between terminal VDD and body ground. Flowchart includes decision points (Yes/No branches) and action boxes (Replace, Display?, OK) leading to various solutions including replacing speedometer, fuse, or gauge, checking wiring, and removing meter and connector sub-harness.
labels: ③With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is 4.0 ~ 6.0V at terminal FV of fuel sender gauge.
④With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is 4.0 ~ 6.0V between terminals 2 and 6 of tachometer connector.
⑤Check for short between terminal VDD and body ground of each meter.
②With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is battery voltage between terminals 8 and 16 of sub-harness (SST).
Bad wiring between fuse and meter
Only speedometer display when other meters disconnected?
Connect meters one by one and check when speedometer display goes out.

content.text: The flowchart contains numbered diagnostic steps:

items: With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is battery voltage between terminals 8 and 16 of sub-harness (SST).
With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is 4.0 ~ 6.0V at terminal FV of fuel sender gauge.
With the ignition S/W at ON position, check that there is 4.0 ~ 6.0V between terminals 2 and 6 of tachometer connector.
Check for short between terminal VDD and body ground of each meter.
